newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Dec 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Dec 31.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Domestic banking, which went through a deep crisis in 1996 should return to better times in 1997, according to financial experts.

- Year-on-year industrial production increased by only 1.5 percent in November, the worst result so far this year. Wages in large industrial firms have increased by 17.2 percent since November of last year.

- Daewoo Avia a.s. sold approximately 4,500 lorries this year, 18 percent more than in 1995. According to preliminary results, 3,900 of these were sold to domestic customers, 500 were exported to Slovakia and the remaining 100 were exported elsewhere.
- Thun Karlovarsky Porcelan a.s. will post a net profit of 75 million crowns, an increase of 250 percent over last year, with a turnover of 1.2 billion crowns.
- Toshulin has founded a daughter company in France. The company will at first be a sales outlet for Toshulin products and will later become a service centre.

- Budejovicky Budvar expects sales of 1.65 billion crowns, output of 1.03 million hectolitres and a gross profit of 320 million crowns in 1996, according to Petr Jansky, the economic manager of the brewery.
PRAVO - In spite of protests from customers, Czech Railways is raising its cargo rates by up to 18 percent, according to the general manager of the railways, Rudolf Mladek.
- Czechinvest was fourth in a survey of the best investment agencies in Europe which is published every year by the Corporate Location magazine in cooperation with Coopers & Lybrand.
